boundary: This dependency index summarizes documented processes. Detailed explanations remain in the referenced guide sections. Verification and failure decisions are authored engineering checks, not executed tests.

entries.title: Evidence retrieval through selected tools
entries.process: Invoke the authorized source with the intended identity, resource and observation period.
entries.verification: Compare returned identifiers and a material measurement with the original source.
entries.on_failure: Report the failed read and withhold conclusions that require that source.

review.inputs: Registered provider endpoint and authentication; space association; selected operation; resource identifiers and observation interval.
narrative: A successful provider registration establishes a connection, not the result of a particular query. The Agent Space association selects the available tool surface. A custom definition can further restrict that surface. At execution time the source still evaluates the actual credentials and request arguments. This is why a missing metric can be a selection, identity, scope or time-window problem rather than an analytical failure.

The mechanism ends with a tool response or an explicit error. Interpreting the response is subsequent work. Keep the source identity and observation interval with the response so that a later summary can be checked against the same measurement.
configuration: Capability Providers → MCP Server → Register; provide HTTPS endpoint and supported authentication.
Agent Space → Capabilities → MCP Servers → Add; select the registered provider and required tools.
Assign the actual tools to the custom definition.
lifecycle: Tools become available to the space, not necessarily every custom definition.
Future access through that association is removed.
Review dependent associations before replacing the registration.
review.controls: Network reachability, authentication, resource permissions and tool selection are separate gates. Use read credentials for this evidence path; mutating tools belong to the directed-action explanation.
review.observable_output: Provider/association configuration and an actual tool result or error; a connection-valid status alone does not prove the intended source query works.
review.undocumented: The platform does not document a universal query planner, response-completeness guarantee or retry/deduplication contract for every connected tool.
test: Use a permitted staging read with a known resource and time interval.
Reproduce one returned measurement with the same source query.
Select an unavailable operation or out-of-scope fixture; require an explicit gap, not a healthy result.

claims.section: Registering an MCP server; Configuring MCP tools; Managing connections
claims.assertion: Registration, association and tool selection are separate; removal and credential replacement have dependent-connection consequences.
A custom agent accesses only its assigned tools.

entries.title: Environment-knowledge construction and refresh
entries.state: Learned relationships and retained context versions
entries.process: Synthesize environment evidence into service, dependency and delivery context for subsequent work.
entries.verification: Check a known changed resource and relationship in the resulting version.
entries.on_failure: Mark stale or inferred relationships; do not substitute the graph for current configuration.

review.inputs: Discovered resources, configuration and observability relationships, connected repository/pipeline context and completed operational work.
narrative: Environment learning turns source evidence into a retained representation. Discovery identifies resources; relationship analysis connects them; learned context describes services and request paths for later work. These products are derived information. They neither replace the deployed configuration nor widen the permission boundary.

Environment understanding, tool-use guidance and monitor history have different refresh conditions. The current memory guide is authoritative for those conditions; the older topology page still uses learned-skill terminology. Requesting regeneration is therefore followed by inspecting the learning result and its version, not by assuming that every dependent view has already changed.
configuration: Connect the relevant accounts and sources; enable Resource Explorer for its documented discovery path.
Use Topology → Regenerate or request the supported update through Chat.
Inspect the resulting environment memory and summary/topology representation.
lifecycle: New derived understanding may be written.
Observe completion and inspect a known changed relationship
The graph is not repaired by granting unrelated write access.
review.controls: Authorization belongs to account roles and tool access. A graph omission does not prove a resource is unreadable, and a graph edge does not prove source completeness.
review.observable_output: Updated context version and a reviewed topology/summary with known changed relationships.
review.undocumented: No universal freshness SLA, complete relationship-detection algorithm or consistency guarantee across all derived views is documented.
test: Identify a harmless staging dependency change with authoritative before/after evidence.
Find that change in the refreshed representation and record the version.
Leave an input unavailable; require the resulting missing or inferred relationship to remain qualified.

claims.section: How topology graphs are created; Resource discovery; Investigation scope beyond topology
claims.assertion: Discovery and relationship inference produce a representation that does not bound investigation permissions.

claims.section: How memory is built and refreshed
claims.assertion: Managed stores have distinct refresh conditions and can be inspected after regeneration.

entries.title: Selective incident-context retrieval
entries.trigger: A task identifies relevant available store descriptions
entries.state: Active stores, entry descriptions, versions and applicable attachments
entries.process: Select a relevant store, inspect its entries and read the content needed by the current task.
entries.verification: Distinguish entry existence, observable retrieval and correctness against current evidence.
entries.on_failure: Continue without history when current evidence suffices. Do not infer retrieval merely from answer wording.

review.inputs: Current task; available store and entry descriptions; active memory content; applicable custom-agent store attachment.
narrative: Retrieval is a selection process, not automatic loading of all history. The agent first sees available store descriptions, then inspects a relevant store and selects entries before reading their content. A useful description exposes the subject and conditions under which an entry matters. A relevant fact hidden behind an unrelated description may never be read.

Operationally, distinguish content production, availability to this execution, selection and diagnostic influence. A previous cause is contextual evidence for a new incident. Current measurements can contradict it. Viewing an old version is also different from restoring a deleted store; the current guide does not establish a general backup or undelete service.
configuration: Knowledge → Memories → select store → View entry; inspect description and version.
Inspect store and entry activation; inspect custom-agent attachments where applicable.
Refine the store/entry description and retest a relevant request.
lifecycle: Content remains but active retrieval is suppressed.
A new immutable version is created.
Store contents are removed; the documented deletion is not reversible.
review.controls: Keep raw incident evidence in its source system. Store access, relevance and answer correctness are separate; memory is not a same-investigation raw-tool cache.
review.observable_output: Entry content/version and, where exposed, a memory read in execution evidence. Output similarity alone does not establish retrieval.
review.undocumented: Embedding model, ranking thresholds, hidden selection policy and model-weight training are not documented by this mechanism.
test: Prepare a harmless known fact and a current observation that contradicts a historical cause.
Record existence, observable retrieval and supported conclusion separately.
Deactivate the entry or remove the applicable attachment and verify that unsupported historical claims are not asserted.

claims.section: How memories work; Activating and deactivating; Deleting a memory store
claims.assertion: Description-led retrieval, immutable versions and activation differ from irreversible custom-store deletion.

entries.title: Corrective investigation feedback
entries.state: Investigation feedback and documented corrective context
entries.process: Record the actual cause separately from routine synthesis of incident history.
entries.verification: Inspect saved feedback and any exposed corrective entry.
entries.on_failure: Keep the verified correction in the incident system when downstream use cannot be observed.

review.inputs: Completed investigation identifier, operator verdict and verified actual cause.
narrative: Feedback supplies a verified correction to a particular investigation. It is not the same input as another occurrence of the alarm and is not the same operation as steering an active investigation. The correction can produce reflection context explaining the discrepancy between the earlier diagnosis and the established cause.

The operator should preserve the evidence for the actual cause independently. Submitting feedback confirms an input was recorded; it does not prove that a later task selected the resulting context. Sharing the feedback with AWS is a separate confirmation decision.
configuration: Completed investigation → Add feedback; supply verdict and actual cause when incorrect, or use the documented Chat path.
Inspect saved feedback and any exposed reflection in Knowledge → Memories.
lifecycle: Inspect the saved latest feedback rather than assuming additive history.
Later use must be evaluated independently.
review.controls: Do not infer production-change authority from a corrective message. Operator evidence, retained correction and optional external sharing are different records.
review.observable_output: Saved feedback and any visible corrective memory; later retrieval is an additional observation.
review.undocumented: The exact latency from submission to reflection availability and a guaranteed recall rate are not established.
test: Use a completed non-production example with a known corrected cause.
Confirm saved correction, then inspect later use only if the execution exposes it.
Supply a different current cause on recurrence; repeating the previous answer is not success.

claims.assertion: Feedback records the actual cause; latest feedback and separate sharing confirmation have distinct effects.
Corrective lessons are retained for future relevant investigations.

entries.title: Standing instruction loading
entries.process: Load standing instructions at session start.
entries.verification: Test a new session against the saved instruction version.
entries.on_failure: Inspect scope and session start time rather than assuming existing sessions received updates.

review.inputs: Saved global and applicable agent-specific AGENTS.md text and a newly starting session.
narrative: Standing instructions are loaded at session initialization. The service includes applicable global and agent-specific content without relying on task-relevance selection. Saving a change affects newly started sessions, not the content already loaded by an existing session.

This makes instructions suitable for persistent reporting conventions. It does not make their content an IAM policy. Use an ordinary output convention as a propagation test and verify actual permissions separately.
configuration: Edit global or relevant managed-agent instructions using the instruction editor exposed by the operator app.
Save, then start a new session.
Retrieved guidance shows both Knowledge → Instructions and Agents → Managed agents → Agent definition. Use the editor present in the deployed interface.
lifecycle: Active session retains its startup content.
review.controls: An instruction cannot grant a tool, change a trust policy or substitute for action approval.
review.observable_output: Saved instruction content and observable behavior in a newly started session.
review.undocumented: Conflict precedence for contradictory global, agent-specific and task instructions is not fully specified; do not assume a precedence order.
test: Add a test-only required heading to a scoped test instruction.
Compare a new session with one started before the change.
A denied tool must remain denied even when the instruction asks to use it.

claims.section: How agent instructions work; Agent type scoping
claims.assertion: Instructions are loaded at session start; existing sessions retain the original content.

entries.title: Runbook applicability and procedural loading
entries.trigger: Applicable task or assigned procedural configuration
entries.state: Skill content, description and agent scope
entries.process: Make the reviewed procedure and its references available to the intended execution.
entries.verification: Test matching and nonmatching requests and inspect exposed procedure or tool-use evidence.
entries.on_failure: Correct applicability or missing tools; stop unsupported steps without implicitly widening permissions.

review.inputs: SKILL.md, applicability description, agent-type targeting and any supporting files; actual tools required by the procedure.
narrative: A skill packages procedural guidance. Its description tells the built-in agent when to select it; targeting limits which agent types can use it. Assigned skills in a custom definition are loaded through that definition, so built-in relevance selection and explicit custom assignment should not be described as identical entry paths.
The procedure still depends on tools that exist and are authorized. Document-only skills do not create a shell. Executable content requires the separately configured Sandbox surface where supported.
configuration: Knowledge → Skills → add a skill with SKILL.md and a concrete applicability description.
Select relevant agent types or assign the skill to the custom definition.
Name real selected operations and expected observations.
lifecycle: Matching task or assigned custom invocation
Check the saved content and actual selection.
Do not assume the procedure remains available.
review.controls: Skill text is guidance, not authorization; executable-code support is feature-specific.
review.observable_output: Saved skill configuration and exposed execution evidence of procedure/tool use.
review.undocumented: The cited guide does not specify relevance thresholds or guarantee a skill-selection event in every execution trace.
test: Provide one request that matches the described symptom and another that does not.
Inspect exposed skill/tool-use evidence and the resulting procedure.
Remove a necessary tool; the task must report the blocked step rather than invent its observation.

claims.assertion: Description, target scope and supported content determine applicability.
Custom definitions load assigned skill documents.

entries.title: Incident routing
entries.process: Link the signal, skip it under configured criteria or proceed with independent investigation.
entries.verification: Inspect the routing decision, reason and resulting investigation identity.
entries.on_failure: Correct routing through the supported unlink or unskip operation.

review.inputs: Incoming external signal, active investigations and configured correlation/skip guidance.
narrative: Triage changes the relationship between a signal and investigation work. Linked signals contribute context to an existing investigation; skipped signals match exclusion criteria; proceed decisions schedule independent work. Routing is therefore not the root-cause result.

Correct a bad relationship at the routing layer. Unlinking or unskipping reschedules independent investigation; changing a hypothesis inside the primary investigation does not repair the original routing decision.
configuration: Connect a supported incident source or webhook and inspect the received event.
Review the relevant correlation or skip skill.
Inspect the triage record and use supported unlink/unskip controls.
lifecycle: Reason is retained without a new investigation.
review.controls: Do not interpret a linked signal as missing work or a skipped signal as proof that the service is healthy.
review.observable_output: Triage outcome, reason and investigation linkage.
review.undocumented: The exact correlation model and an absolute timing guarantee are not specified; a typical lookback is not a universal contract.
test: Submit related and unrelated authorized test events.
Check linkage and reason against known service/time identity.
Deliberately review an incorrect skip criterion and verify the correction changes routing, not resource state.

claims.assertion: Linked, Skipped and Proceed are routing outcomes; supported corrections reschedule independent work.

entries.title: Investigation and operator steering
entries.process: Read observations, examine hypotheses and accept relevant operator steering in the investigation context.
entries.verification: Check conclusions against current observations and identify missing evidence.
entries.on_failure: Retain competing hypotheses or an inconclusive result instead of inventing certainty.

review.inputs: Incident description, start evidence, actual incident time, service scope and connected source access.
narrative: An investigation has its own scope and evidence record. The service gathers observations and develops an explanation; operator steering can add missing or contrary evidence within that record. This describes the observable workflow, not an undisclosed hypothesis-ranking algorithm.

Use the incident timestamp rather than the time the operator happened to open the form. Preserve observations that weaken the leading explanation. A revised analysis is useful only when the supporting evidence also changes.
configuration: Incident Response → start a manual investigation; review details, starting point, UTC incident time, name and priority.
Supply contrary observations within the active investigation.
Review findings and cause; request a mitigation proposal separately.
lifecycle: Analysis can be reconsidered in context.
Later correction is separate from active steering.
review.controls: Steering is not approval for a resource mutation. Missing evidence constrains the conclusion.
review.observable_output: Investigation findings, source observations and any revised conclusion available in the service record.
review.undocumented: No deterministic root-cause accuracy guarantee or complete inference algorithm is published.
test: Use the repository recurring-alarm fixture as a tabletop, not as service telemetry.
Require the explanation to follow the current dependency measurements.
Remove the decisive observation; an inconclusive result is preferable to a fabricated cause.

claims.assertion: Manual scope and operator context drive a separate investigation record.

claims.section: Custom agents compared to built-in capabilities
claims.assertion: Incident response is a built-in path, not a mandatory custom-agent task.

entries.title: Configured custom-agent invocation
entries.process: Execute the selected operational work and retain its invocation trajectory.
entries.verification: Inspect tool arguments, failures and output against the task scope.
entries.on_failure: Mark incomplete output and resolve the failed prerequisite before repeating the run.

review.inputs: Custom definition with system prompt, selected tools, assigned skills and applicable memory access; optional per-run prompt.
narrative: A custom definition persists across executions. Run Now creates a new invocation; an additional prompt supplies context for that run without replacing the system prompt. The execution loads its configured resources, calls available tools and records results in a trajectory.

A definition is not a running job. Likewise, an output artifact is not the invocation itself. Diagnose these objects separately when a report is missing: was an invocation created, did its tools complete, and was the requested output produced?
configuration: Agents → Custom Agents → Create agent; provide goal, approach, constraints and output.
Assign actual tools through the supported configuration path and applicable skills/stores.
Run Now or Run with prompt; open the invocation in History.
lifecycle: An invocation starts or is pending.
Completed evidence is retained; in-flight calls may still finish.
A new record is created; do not assume prior transient context is inherited.
review.controls: Only assigned tools are available. The documented execution page permits one invocation at a time per custom agent.
review.observable_output: Invocation identity, status, tool arguments/results/errors and requested output.
review.undocumented: Exactly-once effects and universal rollback after cancellation are not documented.
test: Create a harmless read-only report over a known staging signal.
Inspect the actual arguments and reconcile a figure in the output.
Cancel a controlled long read; distinguish cancellation from completion of an already-started external call.

claims.assertion: Prompt, selected tools and assigned skills are loaded per invocation.

claims.section: Running; Canceling an invocation; Tool call results
claims.assertion: Runs have history; cancellation preserves completed evidence and may not interrupt in-flight calls.

claims.section: Creating a custom agent using the form
claims.assertion: Creation and tool assignment are separate setup concerns.

entries.title: Schedule-to-invocation creation
entries.process: Create future work under the supported scheduling and concurrency constraints.
entries.verification: Inspect saved timing and actual start; record the observation window independently.
entries.on_failure: Use explicit invocation when timing is critical. Pausing future starts does not cancel current work.

review.inputs: Saved custom agent and valid rate/cron trigger; explicit reporting-window rules in task instructions.
narrative: A trigger schedules future invocation opportunities. It does not specify the observation interval used by a report. The API reference further qualifies the timing: custom-agent schedules use a flexible start window of up to 30 minutes. An expression therefore cannot be presented as an exact delivery deadline.
Pausing the trigger prevents subsequent starts but does not cancel a running invocation. These are two independent control operations and should be inspected separately when retiring recurring work.
configuration: Agents → selected custom agent → Triggers → create; enter a valid rate or cron expression.
Confirm saved expression, next run and actual start.
Pause/delete trigger and, if needed, cancel the current invocation separately.
lifecycle: Eligible future invocation under timing/concurrency constraints.
Trigger is removed; existing execution evidence is separate.
review.controls: Schedule variability, one-at-a-time custom execution and external-call completion are independent constraints.
review.observable_output: Trigger configuration plus actual invocation timing and observation interval.
review.undocumented: Missed-occurrence, overlap queueing and exactly-once delivery behavior are not established by the cited schedule pages.
test: Choose a non-time-critical test report and explicit UTC reporting period.
Compare due time, actual start and the period queried.
Run longer than the interval in an approved test and record actual behavior rather than assuming queued catch-up.

claims.assertion: Rate/cron triggers can be paused or deleted separately from invocations.
The schedule anchors a flexible window of up to 30 minutes.

entries.title: Cross-investigation prevention evaluation
entries.process: Analyze recurring weaknesses and produce improvement proposals.
entries.verification: Trace a proposed theme or improvement to supporting investigations.
entries.on_failure: Keep unsupported patterns as hypotheses and separate proposals from implemented changes.

review.inputs: Recent investigation evidence, existing recommendation backlog and operator disposition feedback.
narrative: Prevention compares incidents to propose changes rather than diagnosing one current alarm. An evaluation produces or updates recommendations; backlog controls describe what the team intends to do with those recommendations. The action that implements a recommendation remains a separate change.

A kept recommendation is not a deployed fix. A recommendation marked implemented is a tracking state, not independent proof of reduced incidents. Retain the implementation and post-change evidence in the normal change process.
configuration: Improvements → Run Now; inspect linked investigations and proposed effect.
Pause recurring evaluation or Stop Evaluation for current work as appropriate.
Use Keep, Discard or Implemented and supply relevant explanation.
lifecycle: Removed from backlog; feedback informs later recommendations.
Tracking status changes; actual implementation must be verified.
review.controls: Priority and estimated effect do not authorize execution or measure realized improvement.
review.observable_output: Recommendation, supporting investigation references, disposition and observed changes.
review.undocumented: Full ranking weights, exact feedback influence and causal benefit attribution are not specified.
test: Review a candidate tied to several known investigations.
Trace the common weakness to its supporting evidence.
A change not deployed must not be reported as completed merely because the recommendation was kept.

claims.assertion: Evaluation control and recommendation disposition are separate; unretained recommendations may age out.

entries.title: Operation-specific directed authorization
entries.trigger: Operator requests an eligible state-changing operation
entries.process: Execute the specific approved operation through its configured authorization path.
entries.verification: Inspect exact approval, attribution and resulting resource state.
entries.on_failure: Stop on a failed authorization gate; use the normal approved engineering process rather than bypassing it.

review.inputs: Eligible exact operation and resource; Agent Space opt-in; target-account elevated role or selected classified tool; operator approval.
narrative: The requested effect passes several gates. Enabling directed actions opens the capability; the target role supplies a permission ceiling; the approval constrains the specific operation and resource. For AWS calls, the service uses scoped credentials and records attribution. None of these steps is replaced by a mitigation recommendation.

External-tool classification is part of the control boundary. A tool marked read-only but implemented as mutating can defeat the intended approval path. Review classification against its real effects and permissions rather than its display name.
configuration: Agent Space settings: enable directed actions; preserve the full preferences map when updating through the API.
Register the elevated role with documented trust including source-identity/session tagging support.
Inspect target and parameters in Chat approval; reject or narrow as needed.
lifecycle: Requests can reach the approval path.
Action success and recovery are separate observations.
review.controls: API preference replacement can reset omitted settings. IAM and service guardrails still apply after approval; tool effects require correct classification.
review.observable_output: Approval details, execution attribution and independently inspected resulting state.
review.undocumented: No universal transactional rollback is documented; approved calls can have effects that outlive the conversation.
test: Use an eligible reversible staging operation under narrow permissions.
Match approval, attribution and target state.
Request a different target or denied operation; it must not inherit the earlier approval.

claims.section: Enabling; Registering elevated role; Categorizing tools; Approving directed actions
claims.assertion: Independent opt-ins, operation-specific approval, preference replacement and classification govern mutation.

entries.title: Candidate release analysis
entries.process: Review the proposed change for the operational risks supported by this preview path.
entries.verification: Match findings to the exact candidate and unresolved dependencies.
entries.on_failure: Treat unsupported repository or feature access as an unmet prerequisite.

review.inputs: Candidate branch/commit and connected repository context; optional managed verification environment.
narrative: Readiness analysis examines a proposed code change. Optional verification builds and exercises the code in a managed environment; it is not a test of whichever production revision happens to be running. A report must therefore identify the candidate and whether verification actually ran.

Insufficient data or permissions are unresolved outcomes, not favorable release decisions. Automated triggers and verification are independently configured, so the presence of a review does not prove that a build/test environment was used.
configuration: Check current release-management Region and repository support.
Configure change-review triggering and automatic verification independently.
Select a verification environment with the required private route and runtime role when needed.
Build dependencies, not unrestricted network access
lifecycle: Analysis record is associated with the candidate.
Test evidence is added when execution succeeds.
Resolve the prerequisite and rerun; do not interpret as clean review.
review.controls: Code verification and active deployed-application testing have different subjects and effects.
review.observable_output: Readiness report, candidate identity, findings and any Tests-tab results.
review.undocumented: Exact risk-scoring thresholds and guaranteed test coverage are not published; feature availability must be checked.
test: Use a non-production candidate with one known behavior change.
Compare findings and executed tests with that revision.
Omit a required build dependency and require an incomplete or failed verification, not a pass.

claims.section: Getting started; Performing a code review; Automatic verification testing
claims.assertion: Review and verification settings are independent; candidate and verification results are inspectable.
Release-management eligibility differs from production operations.

entries.title: Active deployed-application testing
entries.process: Send selected test interactions and retain observed behavior.
entries.verification: Inspect target revision, actual interactions, results and effects.
entries.on_failure: Stop unexpected effects and retain incomplete coverage.

review.inputs: Test profile, deployed URL, UI/API type, test intent and authorized disposable application data.
narrative: Release testing generates a plan from change context or a stated intent and exercises a running application. Its requests can modify data. The relevant identity is therefore the deployed target and its test account, not just the repository branch.

Inspect the actual interactions and results. A generated plan is not executed coverage. This guide uses the documented profile and web-app path rather than copying inconsistent action names from different parts of the retrieved pipeline example.
configuration: Release Manager → Test profiles → Add test profile: name, target URL and UI/API type.
Start testing and provide a bounded test intent.
Use disposable staging data and suppress unintended downstream effects.
lifecycle: Plan generation and active requests begin.
Failures, reproductions and observed behavior become available.
Stop further authorized test activity and inspect target
No automatic undo of prior requests is asserted.
review.controls: Infrastructure read permissions do not make application POST/PUT/DELETE requests harmless.
review.observable_output: Test run, actual target, observed interactions and reproduction details.
review.undocumented: The documentation does not promise exhaustive coverage or transactional rollback of application writes.
test: Prepare a sandboxed checkout endpoint with synthetic records and disabled notifications.
Inspect expected request effects and one known validation error.
An unexpected payment/notification path ends the exercise; do not treat later cancellation as rollback.

claims.section: How release testing works; Defining test profiles; Reviewing results
claims.assertion: Testing sends real requests including writes and reports observed results.
Release testing is a feature-specific preview path.

entries.title: Application-context assembly
entries.process: Read the connected source and documentation relevant to the selected assessment.
entries.verification: Compare source revision and system boundary with the intended subject.
entries.on_failure: Exclude mismatched context and document the resulting assessment limitation.

review.inputs: Connected source/document resources, selected revision or design scope, service-role access and assessment configuration.
narrative: Registration authorizes a provider account; connecting particular resources supplies application-specific evidence. A selected repository can support several assessment types without being independently registered for each. Context assembly must nevertheless use the correct application and revision.

Read access and publication of comments or proposed changes are separate. A context read can help interpret an application without creating a permission to change its repository. The service documentation describes the evidence inputs but not a universal persistent knowledge store or retrieval algorithm for every assessment.
configuration: Integrations: authorize the supported provider account.
Within the intended Agent Space, select repositories or documentation resources.
Review per-repository write options separately from source reads.
lifecycle: Read context becomes available through that association.
A previous result remains tied to its earlier evidence.
Read context does not imply comment or repair permission.
review.controls: Keep application boundary and revision explicit. Private source-control access is separate from private target access.
review.observable_output: Selected resource identity and assessment source/preflight evidence.
review.undocumented: Cross-assessment cache freshness, internal ranking and automatic refresh guarantees are not established.
test: Select a repository and design document that describe one known staging application.
Check that a run identifies that application and revision.
Supply a mismatched design revision and require an explicit mismatch rather than a merged invented architecture.

claims.section: Register once, reuse everywhere; One connection, shared across capabilities
claims.assertion: Registration, resource association and write opt-ins are distinct.

entries.title: Target scope and network access
entries.state: Targets, support paths, exclusions and private route
entries.process: Apply the configured reachability and target rules to assessment access.
entries.verification: Confirm the permitted surface and exclusions in an authorized environment.
entries.on_failure: Stop when scope or owner authorization is unresolved.

review.inputs: Verified target domains, supporting accessible domains, excluded paths, applicable VPC route and authorized test scope.
narrative: The test configuration separates attack targets from supporting navigation and excluded paths. A login provider can be reachable without becoming a vulnerability-testing target. A private route supplies connectivity; it does not widen the scope approved by the application owner.

Treat reachability as a prerequisite. If a target cannot be reached, the missing result is a coverage gap. Broadening the target list or removing an exclusion is a scope change, not a routine network troubleshooting shortcut.
configuration: Create/edit penetration test: select verified target URLs.
Configure excluded paths and the approved VPC connectivity when required.
lifecycle: Reachability is checked before meaningful target testing.
Correct approved route or name resolution
Rerun the prerequisite check without broadening authorization.
A future run has a different assessment surface.
review.controls: Ownership verification and network reachability are not substitutes for owner authorization. Active tests can change application state.
review.observable_output: Preflight outcome and records of the actual target and paths reached.
review.undocumented: The sources do not establish that every reachable path is exercised or that every excluded interaction has a uniform implementation across all targets.
test: Use a non-production target, supporting login host and an explicit excluded fixture path.
Verify target access and intended application role.
A denied path or unresolved target must not produce a claim of assessed coverage.

claims.section: Configure penetration test scope; Configure VPC resources
claims.assertion: Targets, supporting accessible URLs and excluded paths have different purposes.
Failed preflight stops testing and must be inspected separately.

entries.title: Credential resolution and application login
entries.process: Obtain the test credential and apply it to the application.
entries.verification: Check the actual application identity and protected route, not only credential retrieval.
entries.on_failure: Mark protected paths unassessed when login fails.

review.inputs: Credential strategy, permitted source resource, access URL, application login instructions and representative test identity.
narrative: Authentication has two stages: retrieve or obtain the credential, then apply it to the application. Secrets Manager or Lambda can succeed while application login fails. The credential name therefore needs to remain associated with the role and protected paths actually reached.

The login instructions describe how to apply the returned value, not how to bypass an inaccessible identity provider. Use the credential mechanisms currently exposed in the test configuration; older and newer retrieved documentation differ on some authentication options. Do not treat that difference as evidence that every deployed interface supports the same flow.
configuration: Choose direct input or a documented AWS-native strategy in the test credential configuration.
For Secrets Manager, scope GetSecretValue and DescribeSecret; for Lambda, scope InvokeFunction.
Provide access URL and login instructions; verify the resulting identity before interpreting findings.
lifecycle: Credential value is obtained or resolution fails.
Application session succeeds or login fails.
Source success does not establish current application access.
review.controls: The credential guide requires same-account Secrets Manager/Lambda resources and a credential Lambda completing within 30 seconds. Never place secrets in the documentation examples.
review.observable_output: Resolution and login evidence plus actual application role; secret contents are not required in retained review evidence.
review.undocumented: The documentation does not establish one universal authentication policy, retry algorithm or credential-refresh behavior for all applications.
test: Use a disposable customer-role account and a known protected staging route.
Record resolution success and the actual role reaching the route.
Use an expired test credential: distinguish source-read success from failed login.

claims.section: Use advanced setting; Configure multiple credentials
claims.assertion: Resource retrieval and application login are separate; strategy-specific permissions and limits apply.

entries.title: Successful login-procedure reuse
entries.state: Retained login procedure and reuse setting
entries.process: Reuse learned navigation where the setting and current login flow permit it.
entries.verification: Distinguish successful login from observable procedure reuse.
entries.on_failure: Retest a changed login flow; failed login is not a clean assessment.

review.inputs: Configured test credentials, a successfully discovered login flow and the Login Optimization setting.
narrative: Successful navigation produces a reusable login procedure. Later login sessions can read that procedure instead of rediscovering the path. Reuse concerns navigation; it does not establish that an old credential remains valid or that the application still assigns the intended role.

This is separate from finding personalization and vulnerability revalidation. A changed login flow calls for a fresh authentication check, while a changed vulnerability calls for assessment or revalidation. Switching off reuse is not a documented deletion of learned material.
configuration: Configure a credential and complete a successful login.
Inspect Login Optimization in the penetration-test configuration; the documentation identifies it as enabled by default.
On later sessions, verify authenticated identity independently from any observable reuse.
lifecycle: A reusable skill file is produced.
Reuse stops; retained learning is preserved.
review.controls: Test current credentials and role on each relevant run. Retained navigation is not a general-purpose incident memory.
review.observable_output: Authenticated session and, where exposed, evidence of reuse. Do not infer reuse solely from faster execution.
review.undocumented: No independent public CRUD API or guaranteed invalidation policy for the saved login skill is established.
test: Use an authorized multistep staging login.
Compare first and later logins while verifying the same application role.
Change the login form; failure to reach the protected route remains a coverage gap.

claims.assertion: Successful navigation produces a skill reused in later sessions/runs; disabling reuse preserves learning.

entries.title: Saved assessment and independent execution
entries.process: Execute against the current configured target and retain an independent result.
entries.verification: Record actual revision, roles, exclusions, limit and incomplete areas.
entries.on_failure: Treat incomplete or failed execution as a coverage gap, not a pass.

review.inputs: Saved penetration-test configuration, current target deployment, credentials, exclusions and execution/work limit.
narrative: A saved penetration-test configuration is reusable; each execution has its own record and findings. Saving the configuration does not freeze a deployment that continues to change. Identify the deployed revision and current credentials for every run.

Execution begins with prerequisite checks before assessment work. A preflight failure is neither a successful clean assessment nor evidence that the target contains no vulnerabilities. The assessment record should retain incomplete areas along with findings.
configuration: Penetration tests → create: configure target, role, credentials, network and source context.
Choose the supported save-only or create-and-execute action.
Open the run overview, preflight/logs and findings.
lifecycle: Resolve prerequisite and start a new run
No successful runtime coverage is established.
Further execution uses a new run, not rewritten evidence.
review.controls: Work limits, test scope and owner authorization must remain explicit; budget limits do not guarantee a particular coverage level.
review.observable_output: Run identity, actual target context, logs, discovered/tested endpoints and findings.
review.undocumented: The documented interface does not expose the complete assessment-planning or vulnerability-discovery algorithm.
test: Use a deliberately limited staging target and record its deployed revision.
Inspect actual reached paths and completed phases.
Make a required target unreachable; require a preflight failure or explicit coverage gap.

claims.section: Penetration testing: reusable configurations with independent executions
claims.assertion: One configuration supports separate runs and new findings.
Saving, executing and preflight outcomes are different stages.

entries.title: Finding evidence inspection
entries.process: Expose the affected context and supporting reproduction or source evidence for review.
entries.verification: Give the finding a disposition using evidence, impact and application-owner context.
entries.on_failure: Preserve uncertainty and obtain missing evidence before closure.

review.inputs: Finding identifier, current/original attributes, validation evidence, assessment revision and application-owner context.
narrative: A finding combines an observation with an interpretation of risk. Inspect the supporting request, response or source evidence before accepting that interpretation. The findings view can hide unverified items, so the visible count depends on the active filter.

Editing a finding changes its recorded attributes; it does not repair the application. The separately documented Findings Personalization mechanism can also influence later similar findings. Read the original and latest values when determining whether a change reflects new vulnerability evidence or a revised organizational preference.
configuration: Completed/in-progress run → Findings → select finding and trace its actions/logs.
Review the unverified-findings filter before counting results.
Review current and original values where edits exist.
lifecycle: Confidence and supported impact can be assessed.
Latest attributes change; original view remains available.
An edited status does not establish deployed remediation.
review.controls: Generated reproduction scripts require review and an authorized target before execution. Finding counts and severity alone do not establish risk or coverage.
review.observable_output: Finding identity, supporting evidence, original/latest values and a reviewer disposition.
review.undocumented: No calibrated probability interpretation of confidence or exhaustive false-negative rate is established.
test: Use the synthetic authorization-finding fixture for a tabletop.
Trace the claim to the supplied identity, request and affected revision.
Hide/unhide unverified findings and verify that changed visibility is not reported as remediation.

claims.section: Default confidence filter; Review finding details; View original agent version
claims.assertion: Evidence, display filtering and original/latest attributes are distinct review surfaces.

related_mechanisms.condition: Findings Personalization was enabled at test start and eligible edits are available; it changes finding attributes, not application state.

entries.title: Repository repair proposal
entries.trigger: Accepted finding and configured source access
entries.process: Create a supported patch or pull request for engineering review.
entries.verification: Inspect revision, tests and unrelated changes before accepting the proposal.
entries.on_failure: Leave a failed or rejected proposal unfinished; merge is not deployment.

review.inputs: Finding, eligible connected repository or S3 source, configured remediation permission and selected source context.
narrative: Remediation produces a proposed source change. Current provider guidance describes pull/merge requests for eligible private repositories and a downloadable diff for S3 sources. Older retrieved text describes a narrower provider/public-repository path; do not generalize either wording to unsupported provider writes.
The proposal remains separate from review, merge, deployment and finding revalidation. Preserve the original finding relationship through those steps, including any linked Jira record.
configuration: Enable remediation in the administrative configuration and select the appropriate repositories/source.
From the finding, choose Remediate code or use the configured automatic proposal path.
Inspect proposal/diff and its tests before normal deployment.
lifecycle: Attempt and proposed change are produced.
Accept, revise or reject without implying deployment.
Test the actual target rather than the branch.
review.controls: Read-only source access does not grant proposal-write permission. A pull request is not an automatically deployed fix.
review.observable_output: Remediation status, linked proposal/diff and original finding identity.
review.undocumented: No universal guarantee of successful repair, regression coverage or automatic deployment is provided.
test: Use a known authorized fixture finding and isolated test repository.
Inspect intended diff, tests and unrelated changes.
A failing build or undeployed merge must keep verification incomplete.

claims.assertion: Current guidance distinguishes private-repository proposals and S3 diffs.
Repository writes are separately configured and provider-limited.

entries.title: Selected finding replay and lineage
entries.trigger: Repair deployed to the authorized target
entries.state: Original finding and separate revalidation job
entries.process: Repeat selected finding-validation steps under current test conditions.
entries.verification: Verify reached identity, deployed repair and linked result.
entries.on_failure: Record authentication or environment failure as inconclusive verification.

review.inputs: Completed test findings, deployed repair on the original target and current authentication configuration.
narrative: Revalidation repeats validation steps for selected existing findings and creates a separate job. The original finding remains available and the result links back to it. This is targeted replay, not new vulnerability discovery.

An Active result means reproduction succeeded. Resolved means the service could not reproduce the issue during this replay. The engineering review must still confirm that the intended identity and path were reached; a failed login cannot demonstrate a repaired authorization check.
configuration: Deploy the reviewed repair to the environment originally tested.
Completed run → Multiselect findings for revalidation → select findings → Revalidate findings.
Open the job, original finding and revalidation history.
lifecycle: Interpret within reached identity and scope.
A further linked job records a new attempt.
review.controls: Full assessments remain necessary for broader changes; replay does not certify whole-application security.
review.observable_output: Linked job and per-finding replay result; linked Jira issues can receive result comments.
review.undocumented: No exactly-once callback or universal guarantee distinguishing every environmental failure from non-reproduction is established.
test: Use a deployed repair with a known test identity and retained original finding.
Check the reached identity and link to the replay result.
Break authentication in a controlled test; record verification as inconclusive rather than celebrating non-reproduction.

claims.section: Select findings; Interpret results; Trace history
claims.assertion: Replay has separate job identity, selected scope and preserved original finding.

entries.title: Requirement applicability and evaluation
entries.trigger: Eligible review with requirement mode enabled
entries.process: Evaluate supplied evidence against applicable requirements.
entries.verification: Check compliant, violating and inapplicable examples.
entries.on_failure: Revise ambiguous applicability; do not treat a pack as a compliance certificate.

review.inputs: Enabled pack, requirement applicability/compliance definitions and eligible source/design review evidence.
narrative: Requirement evaluation first needs a criterion that applies to the subject. The compliance assessment then compares the supplied evidence with that criterion. Missing evidence is not the same as a demonstrated violation or an inapplicable requirement.

Packs are shared policy configuration. Enabling, disabling or editing one affects future eligible reviews, not the historical conclusions of reviews already completed. This shared reach makes requirement maintenance a cross-application change.
configuration: Security requirements → chosen pack → inspect applicability, compliance criteria and optional remediation guidance.
Enable the reviewed pack and select requirement evaluation in the eligible review mode.
Review the stated reason for applicability and result.
lifecycle: Criteria apply to new eligible reviews.
review.controls: Framework labels and managed packs are not compliance certification; applicability is part of the evaluated claim.
review.observable_output: Requirement-linked result and explanation, including missing-data or inapplicable distinctions where exposed.
review.undocumented: Full semantic evaluation rules and a deterministic false-positive/false-negative guarantee are not documented.
test: Prepare compliant, violating and deliberately inapplicable examples for one requirement.
Check applicability before the compliance verdict.
Remove decisive design evidence; require an insufficient-evidence interpretation, not assumed compliance.

claims.section: Overview; Enable or disable a pack
claims.assertion: Enabled packs govern future eligible reviews and have distinct applicability/compliance fields.
Design reviews distinguish Insufficient data and Not applicable from compliance/violation.

entries.title: Requirement-pack regeneration
entries.trigger: Policy documents are submitted for requirement generation
entries.state: Existing custom pack and generated replacement
entries.process: Replace pack contents from the selected policy documents for subsequent review.
entries.verification: Compare with approved policy and prior manually added requirements.
entries.on_failure: Do not enable an unreviewed replacement; keep authoritative source in Git.

review.inputs: Documents submitted for a custom requirement pack. The team reviews the policy source and replacement before enabling the pack.
narrative: Generation reads policy documents and constructs structured requirements. Running it again for an existing pack replaces the requirements; it is not an append operation. A successful generation therefore establishes a proposed replacement, not approval of every generated rule.
Reconcile overlapping policies before submission. Review applicability and technical criteria afterward, and explicitly compare the replacement with any manual entries that existed before the upload.
configuration: Security requirements → Custom packs → choose/create the intended pack.
Upload supported documents and choose Generate requirements; acknowledge replacement when applicable.
Review/edit resulting requirements before enabling the pack for later assessments.
lifecycle: Existing requirements, including manual ones, are replaced.
The documented workflow blocks another upload until processing finishes.
New eligible reviews use the accepted configuration.
review.controls: Keep authoritative policy and reviewed configuration in Git; do not treat a generated pack as the only source of policy.
review.observable_output: Generated requirement definitions and prospective pack state.
review.undocumented: Automatic merge of old/manual rules and transactional rollback are not documented.
test: Use a disposable pack containing one manual rule and an approved small policy fixture.
Compare resulting criteria with source and prior contents.
Confirm replacement behavior without using a production policy pack.

claims.section: Generate requirements; Replace requirements with a new upload
claims.assertion: Generation replaces existing pack contents and requires review before use.

entries.title: Full-source or change-focused code assessment
entries.process: Analyze selected source in the configured vulnerability and requirement modes.
entries.effect: Source analysis; optional comments separately configured
entries.verification: Match results to the revision and record unassessed scope.
entries.on_failure: Obtain a current result when revision or trigger behavior makes prior evidence stale.

review.inputs: Exact source revision, full/differential scope, selected review modes, enabled requirements and source-access role.
narrative: Full-source and change-focused reviews use related analysis but different evidence boundaries. Preflight must first obtain the source and prepare the environment. A failure at that stage is not a clean scan.

Repository-event settings and optional comments are distinct from a manually started full review. The documented filtering file is read from the repository main branch, so changing it only in an unmerged branch may not change the current review behavior.
configuration: Web app → Code reviews → create: select sources and role; Start review.
Select vulnerability findings, requirement evaluation or both.
Review supported provider triggers and .awssecurityagent/filtering.md on the main branch.
lifecycle: Fix access and start a new run
review.controls: Read analysis, posted comments and proposed repairs are different effects. Excluded source is unassessed, not verified safe.
review.observable_output: Preflight results, reviewed revision, findings and any configured provider comments.
review.undocumented: No complete vulnerability-discovery algorithm or exhaustive language/framework coverage is inferred from a successful run.
test: Review a known source fixture with exact commit identity.
Check that findings reference the expected revision and modes.
Deny source access or exclude a known fixture path; retain the resulting assessment gap.

claims.section: Create and run a code review; Review findings
claims.assertion: Source preflight precedes analysis and has inspectable failure outcomes.

claims.section: How code review works; Filtering findings
claims.assertion: Change-trigger and main-branch filtering behavior are distinct configuration paths.

entries.title: Point-in-time design assessment
entries.process: Assess the submitted design against relevant criteria.
entries.verification: Separate missing evidence from demonstrated violation.
entries.on_failure: Use the documented new-review or clone path for changed design material.

review.inputs: Current design documents, application context and enabled security criteria.
narrative: Design review evaluates a submitted description of the system. It does not observe whether the deployed implementation actually enforces that description. The review must distinguish a requirement violation from missing design evidence.
Its lifecycle is one-off rather than a reusable test configuration. Clone or create a new review for revised material so the earlier result remains attributable to its original documents.
configuration: Select the design-review workflow and current design material.
Open findings by requirement and read the compliance explanation.
Clone/create a new review with updated material.
lifecycle: Prepare a new assessment, not a fabricated pass.
New point-in-time result; original review remains separate.
review.controls: Design compliance is not implementation verification.
review.observable_output: Reviewed files, requirement result and explanation.
review.undocumented: Automatic refresh of existing design reviews and continuous synchronized system models are not documented.
test: Use a design fixture with an explicit identity boundary and one omitted control.
Verify the difference between violation and insufficient evidence.
Revise the document without rerunning; the old result must not be presented as a new assessment.

claims.assertion: Design reviews have a different one-off lifecycle.
Missing evidence and non-compliance differ; cloning creates a new review.

entries.title: System-model construction and threat analysis
entries.process: Construct the system model and examine threats to its flows and boundaries.
entries.verification: Review inferred boundaries before interpreting individual threats.
entries.on_failure: Correct input scope when the model represents the wrong system.

review.inputs: Scope documents, selected sources or both, application boundary and service role.
narrative: Scope documents express what should be modeled; source code supplies context for the current system. The output includes a system overview and threats derived for that representation. Review the system boundary and flows before accepting the threats built on them.
A model of the wrong system can produce plausible but irrelevant threats. Correct the scope or source mismatch and run again rather than dismissing every downstream item individually.
configuration: Threat models → Create threat model: title, scope documents and/or sources, service role and optional log group.
Start run; inspect Preflight and Logs.
Inspect Overview before Threats; review evidence and recommendations.
lifecycle: Preflight and analysis create a system model.
Accept, resolve or dismiss findings with rationale.
New result reflects the intended subject.
review.controls: Inferred relationships require owner review; threat status is not proof that a mitigation is deployed.
review.observable_output: System overview, threat statements, classifications, evidence and recommendations.
review.undocumented: The exhaustive threat-generation strategy and completeness of inferred flows are not published.
test: Provide a small design with a known trust boundary and supporting source.
Check that the overview reflects the known boundary.
Use a deliberately stale scope document; identify the mismatch before interpreting threat counts.

claims.section: Create and run a threat model; Review threats
claims.assertion: Scope documents and source context have distinct roles; overview and threats are reviewable.

entries.title: Pipeline invocation and result observation
entries.process: Start and observe the supported assessment independently of the pipeline runner.
entries.verification: Retain revision and run identity and apply an explicit team gate to incomplete results.
entries.on_failure: Block or escalate under the declared gate; missing evidence is not success.

review.inputs: Existing penetration-test configuration with CI/CD mode, source connection, pipeline OIDC identity and deployed change identifiers.
narrative: The pipeline step starts and observes a server-side test of a deployed change. It does not create the application or replace the saved assessment scope, and it does not run the penetration-testing engine inside the delivery runner.

Configure the release decision before enabling the integration. Invocation failure, unfinished assessment and a completed result above the selected severity threshold need distinct handling. This decision policy is authored team behavior, not a claim that every pipeline fails closed automatically.
configuration: Verify target and create a test with current credentials/network scope; enable CI/CD mode and record space/test IDs.
Configure the provider-specific OIDC path and supported integration step.
Set accepted threshold and explicit behavior for missing/incomplete results.
lifecycle: Runner completion is not yet assessment completion.
Promote, block or escalate using that result and revision.
review.controls: This preview path is post-deployment assessment, not pull-request static analysis.
review.observable_output: Pipeline execution, deployed change, assessment job and applied promotion decision.
review.undocumented: Exactly-once invocation, universal timeout behavior and identical provider semantics are not established.
test: Use a non-production pipeline with known deployed revision and saved assessment.
Retain the server job ID with the gate result.
Simulate unavailable/incomplete result; follow the declared blocking/escalation rule rather than passing silently.

claims.assertion: The integration invokes an existing configured test, uses OIDC and observes server-side work.

entries.title: Finding publication to Jira
entries.process: Publish supported issue or comment content to the configured project.
entries.verification: Inspect actual project audience and original finding linkage.
entries.on_failure: Keep the finding owned locally while resolving publication failure.

review.inputs: Connected Jira Cloud site, permitted project/actions, selected finding and reviewed disclosure scope.
narrative: A site registration supplies authorization; a project connection chooses where the Agent Space can create issues or comments. Creating an issue publishes a finding into an external system with its own audience and lifecycle.

The link matters later: remediation proposals and revalidation outcomes can be attached to the same issue through supported behavior. Removing the integration stops future actions but does not remove tickets already created.
configuration: Integrations → Add integration → Jira; authorize the Forge app and registration.
Within Agent Space select project and allowed create/comment actions.
Select finding(s) and create issues in a project permitting the Task type.
lifecycle: External record and finding relationship created.
No further action through that integration; existing issues remain.
review.controls: Issue creation and comment permission are separate. Do not import FinOps approval behavior into Security Agent.
review.observable_output: Actual issue/comment in the intended project and preserved finding link.
review.undocumented: Automatic duplicate suppression and transactional rollback across AWS and Jira are not established.
test: Use a restricted test project and a non-sensitive finding fixture.
Check audience, issue type and finding link.
Revoke comment permission; distinguish publication failure from assessment failure and avoid blind duplicate retries.

claims.section: Connecting projects to an Agent Space
claims.assertion: Create and comment actions are selected per project.
The selected project must allow Task and receives one issue per selected finding.
Previously created issues are not deleted with the integration.

entries.title: Source-backed cost analysis
entries.trigger: Bounded cost, forecast, coverage or recommendation question
entries.process: Read the relevant upstream service and interpret its returned evidence.
entries.verification: Reconcile a material result using the same dates, metric, scope and dimensions.
entries.on_failure: Withhold unsupported numerical or causal conclusions and identify missing sources.

review.inputs: Question, dates, cost metric, scope, dimensions, currency and permissions to the relevant source service.
narrative: The agent queries the service that owns the requested evidence. Historical cost, forecasts, commitment coverage, anomaly records, optimization recommendations and change events are different inputs. Combining them in one conversation does not turn projected savings into observed spend.

The analytical result must preserve the query basis. First reconcile amounts, then examine operational evidence for an explanation. A nearby change event is a lead; numerical contribution and causal attribution remain different claims.
configuration: Enable required upstream services and inspect the agent data role.
State complete periods, metric, filters and grouping.
Identify which source supplied a forecast, anomaly or recommendation.
lifecycle: Source result or access failure returned.
New result is not comparable unless the basis is reconciled.
No infrastructure change is authorized by retrieval.
review.controls: The service summarizes recommendations from optimization services; it does not independently calculate its own underlying optimization analysis.
review.observable_output: Returned figures, query basis and source/tool evidence.
review.undocumented: The source guides do not specify the query-planning algorithm. Queries with different dates, metrics or filters are not directly comparable.
test: Use the supplied synthetic cost fixture or a read-only query in an authorized account.
Reconcile components to the total under identical periods and metric.
Change metric or period deliberately; identify why the totals are not comparable.

claims.assertion: Cost Explorer, anomaly detection, optimization services and CloudTrail supply distinct evidence.
Recommendations are upstream analysis; anomaly causality remains investigative.

entries.title: Uploaded reference-file use
entries.process: Read the maintained mapping or reporting convention during relevant work.
entries.verification: Verify a known mapping and expose unmapped records.
entries.on_failure: Keep unassigned values visible and update the authoritative file deliberately.

review.inputs: Approved non-sensitive organization mapping or report convention in a supported active file.
narrative: Uploaded context is maintained outside the conversation. The agent can read the file but cannot rewrite or delete it by conversational instruction. A request to forget a preference therefore does not modify a conflicting account-owner mapping in an uploaded file.

Soft deletion removes a file from active context and Restore makes it active again. This is a documented reversible lifecycle for files, not a claim that every other retained object supports restoration.
configuration: Context files workspace: upload TXT, CSV, JSON, Markdown, HTML or YAML within documented size limits.
Update the governed source and intentionally replace the active uploaded representation.
lifecycle: Memory is a separate representation and may need separate correction.
review.controls: Files are visible to users with access to the agent. Do not upload credentials or sensitive personal information.
review.observable_output: File state and correct application of a known identifier mapping.
review.undocumented: File-versus-memory precedence and exact internal retrieval ranking are not specified.
test: Upload a harmless mapping for a fictitious account label.
Ask a question requiring that mapping and inspect attribution.
Soft-delete it and test again; restoring the file is distinct from remembering a new preference.

claims.section: Supported file types; Manage context files
claims.assertion: Files are agent-read-only, size-limited and support soft deletion/restoration.
File removal and other object lifecycles differ.

entries.title: Cross-session preference retention
entries.trigger: Conversation preferences, corrections or task outcomes; explicit remember, update or forget requests
entries.process: Apply retained preferences to subsequent sessions.
entries.verification: Test a later conversation separately from reference-file retrieval.
entries.on_failure: State material query choices explicitly when retention is uncertain.

review.inputs: Conversation preferences, corrections, task outcomes, and explicit requests to remember, update or forget information within the instance.
narrative: Conversational memory retains preferences and corrections for later work in the same instance. It is not the current conversation transcript and is not an uploaded file. An explicit remember, update or forget instruction targets this retained representation.

Test it across sessions rather than immediately repeating the fact in the same conversation. Also inspect whether an active reference file supplies the same information; otherwise successful file use can be mistaken for memory recall.
configuration: Ask the agent to remember or update one non-sensitive preference.
Ask it to forget the specific retained fact.
Use a later session without restating the test fact.
lifecycle: Retained context can influence later work.
Persistent instance data is separate from ephemeral runtime.
review.controls: Each instance isolates its retained content; no shared organization-wide memory is inferred.
review.observable_output: Observed later use of a controlled fact, qualified when no direct memory-inspection evidence is exposed.
review.undocumented: Internal schema, selection precedence and complete deletion of historical conversation occurrences are not established by a forget request.
test: Use a fictitious reporting preference absent from uploaded files.
Test a later session, then change the preference and test again.
Forget it; do not claim that earlier reports or conversation history were erased.

claims.assertion: Remember, update and forget govern retained preferences/corrections.
Instance isolation and memory updates differ from conversation retention.

entries.title: Conversation compaction
entries.state: Summary of older material and recent full messages
entries.process: Summarize older context while continuing the conversation.
entries.verification: Restate the current query basis and unresolved questions.
entries.on_failure: Reconstruct critical constraints from authoritative records instead of assuming verbatim recall.

review.inputs: Growing conversation approaching the model context window.
narrative: Compaction changes the context supplied to continued conversation. Older material is summarized while recent messages remain in full. It preserves a working representation of key decisions, not a verbatim copy of every earlier turn.

Keep a material cost question explicit after a long exchange: period, metric, filters and unresolved assumptions. Restating those choices is an engineering safeguard, not a control that changes the undocumented compaction algorithm.
configuration: Automatic; no administrator threshold or manual compaction switch is established by the cited guide.
Restate critical query constraints and reference authoritative outputs.
lifecycle: Recent messages and summary guide subsequent work.
Do not infer verbatim recall from a fluent answer.
review.controls: Compaction is not durable preference management or deletion of stored conversation history.
review.observable_output: Continued conversation and the constraints it actually applies; a direct compaction event may not be exposed.
review.undocumented: Thresholds, summary-selection rules and lossless retention are not documented.
test: Use a non-sensitive long conversation with a recorded query contract.
Check whether later analysis retains the period and metric.
Where detail is missing, restore it explicitly and label compaction itself unobserved if no service signal exists.

claims.assertion: Automatic summarization replaces older context while recent messages remain in full.

entries.title: Queued task execution and observation
entries.state: Task status, source results and outputs
entries.process: Run queued work and retain its separate execution evidence.
entries.verification: Match completed results to task identity and requested scope.
entries.on_failure: Distinguish absent, queued and failed tasks before retrying.

review.inputs: Explicit task request or automation invocation, prompt and permitted data/context.
narrative: An ordinary question can be answered in the conversation. A task is created when explicitly requested or through an automation. The task has its own queue position, execution and output, so a chat acknowledgement is not completion evidence.
All documented task types share a queue. Inspect whether work was never created, remains queued, failed during analysis or completed but failed to publish. Those failures require different actions.
configuration: Ask explicitly to create a task, or Tasks → Create tasks.
Inspect Tasks/history and actual tool results.
Use supported cancellation for current work; control recurring automation separately.
lifecycle: Cancellation does not delete task history.
review.controls: Cancelling work is not rollback of prior external publication.
review.observable_output: Task identity, execution status, source calls, outputs and separate delivery outcome.
review.undocumented: Queue order, fairness, exactly-once processing and guaranteed cancellation of every in-flight action are not specified.
test: Create a report task using non-sensitive inputs with an explicit date range.
Trace its identity from request to resulting output.
Cancel controlled work and distinguish preserved history from a deleted task.

claims.assertion: Tasks are explicit and run through a shared queue rather than blocking the conversation.
Cancellation and record removal are different lifecycle operations.

entries.title: Scheduled task creation
entries.process: Create a new task on each applicable scheduled occurrence.
entries.verification: Inspect trigger and the actual task's reporting window separately.
entries.on_failure: Disable future starts and control already-created work separately.

review.inputs: Recurring prompt, explicit schedule and timezone, observation-window rule and optional destination.
narrative: A recurring request creates an automation. Each eligible occurrence creates separate work; the automation is not the historical report. Keep the schedule and reporting basis distinct so a delayed task still queries the intended complete period.

Disabling an automation controls future starts. Existing tasks and distributed artifacts retain their own lifecycle. When replacing recurring work, inspect old automations to avoid running both definitions unintentionally.
configuration: Describe the recurring work and schedule in conversation.
Open Automations and confirm the actual saved schedule and prompt.
Stop future occurrences through the automation control.
review.controls: Unattended publication has destination-specific authorization; recurrence is not a universal approval bypass for unrelated actions.
review.observable_output: Automation configuration and individual task histories with their queried periods.
review.undocumented: Exact missed-run and timezone-resolution behavior must be inspected; the guide does not establish a universal timing SLA.
test: Create a non-sensitive recurring report only after an on-demand trial.
Inspect saved timing and the first task observation window.
Disable the automation and confirm future creation stops without assuming prior artifacts disappear.

claims.assertion: Schedules create automations and new tasks; disabling/deleting stops recurring work.
Automations and task records have distinct lifecycles.

entries.title: Anomaly-event matching and task creation
entries.state: Managed rule, automation and queued task
entries.process: Match the supported event to its configured response prompt.
entries.effect: Task creation; publication is a separate configured step
entries.verification: Trace event, automation, task, analysis and destination result independently.
entries.on_failure: Inspect monitor conditions and rule permissions before changing the analytical prompt.

review.inputs: Cost Anomaly Detection monitor, required managed EventBridge permissions, condition, response prompt and optional destination.
narrative: The event path begins in Cost Anomaly Detection. The service creates a managed rule, matches the configured condition and creates a task using the saved prompt. Analysis and delivery occur after task creation; they are not evidence that matching itself was correct.

Trace the chain one object at a time. A monitor event with no task points toward rule or condition configuration. A completed analysis with no message points toward destination publication. Changing the analytical prompt does not repair an absent event subscription.
configuration: Configure a monitor and the agent-role EventBridge permissions.
Describe monitor/scope, threshold and desired response in Chat.
Inspect automation status, last-triggered information, created task and destination result.
