lifecycle: No future task from that automation; old records remain.
review.controls: The documented preview event source is Cost Anomaly Detection, not arbitrary events. External publication requires its configured destination.
review.observable_output: Monitor/event identity, automation, task, source analysis and any actual message.
review.undocumented: Event deduplication keys, ordering and universal delivery/retry guarantees are not established.
test: Use a controlled event fixture for tabletop tracing; do not manufacture production spend.
Verify all chain identities against available service records during an authorized test.
A missing message must be localized to absent task, failed analysis or failed delivery rather than reported as one undifferentiated error.

claims.section: Prerequisites; Verify and manage the automation
claims.assertion: Monitor, managed-rule permissions and saved condition create a traceable automation/task path.
The supported preview trigger is a cost-anomaly event.

entries.title: Report generation and revision
entries.state: Report artifact, originating conversation or task, and query basis
entries.process: Format supported output and revise it without silently changing analytical scope.
entries.verification: Compare displayed figures and period with the reviewed source analysis.
entries.on_failure: Do not distribute an artifact that no longer matches its query basis.

review.inputs: Cost-report request, authorized source access, query parameters, output format and optional report template.
narrative: Report generation retrieves source data, builds the requested presentation and returns an artifact. A visual quality pass concerns presentation defects; it is not an independent reconciliation of the underlying financial interpretation.
A follow-up can revise the artifact. Keep the analytical basis explicit when revising it: changing a title or chart layout should not silently change period, cost metric or grouping.
configuration: Specify report audience, source period, metric, required sections and supported format; default is HTML.
Open/download from Artifacts and compare figures to source results.
Reference the existing report in a follow-up and state whether the query basis may change.
lifecycle: Downloaded or published copies require separate handling.
review.controls: Formatting and completion status do not establish numerical accuracy; distribution is a separate effect.
review.observable_output: Report artifact and its source conversation or task. Record the query parameters and output identity used for reconciliation.
review.undocumented: An immutable artifact-version API and universal external-copy deletion are not established by the report guide.
test: Generate a report from the small supplied synthetic cost fixture.
Reconcile displayed components and totals to the fixture.
Revise layout only and verify that period, metric and numbers did not change.

claims.assertion: Reports are artifacts, default to HTML and can be revised through follow-up.
Artifacts and other retained objects have distinct controls.

entries.title: Invocation-dependent Jira approval
entries.process: Request approval interactively or on demand; use setup authorization for scheduled or event-driven actions.
entries.verification: Inspect invocation type, action details, destination and resulting issue or comment.
entries.on_failure: Stop incorrect destinations. Do not expect an interactive prompt to protect an unattended automation.

review.inputs: Account Jira registration, per-instance project connection, supported action, payload and invocation mode.
narrative: Jira approval depends on how the action starts. Chat and on-demand tasks present issue/comment details for confirmation; a scheduled or event automation uses authorization established during setup. The same destination does not imply the same per-run approval behavior.

After approval or preauthorization, inspect the actual external record. A successful analysis is not a successful issue creation, and a retry after an uncertain response can create duplicates unless the operator checks the existing project records.
configuration: Authorize the Jira Cloud integration, then bind the approved project to this instance.
Review project, issue/comment body and target shown for approval.
Review action and audience before enabling recurrence/event handling.
lifecycle: Publication executes without a per-run approval prompt.
Avoid assuming an unobserved response means no issue exists.
review.controls: Supported actions do not include arbitrary issue-field changes, deletion or Jira workflow management.
review.observable_output: Actual issue/comment, intended project and task action history.
review.undocumented: Exactly-once external publication and automatic duplicate suppression are not documented.
test: Use a restricted Jira Cloud test project and non-sensitive payload.
Compare interactive approval with a separately reviewed automation test.
Deny project access and verify a publication failure does not erase or falsely complete the analysis record.

claims.section: Jira issue creation and comment addition
claims.assertion: Approval differs between interactive/on-demand and automated invocation.
Project connections and supported actions limit the effect.

entries.title: Direct Slack publication
entries.process: Post to the configured channel without a per-message approval prompt.
entries.verification: Review audience before invocation and inspect delivery afterward.
entries.on_failure: Keep analysis completion separate from delivery failure; posting does not establish channel-reading capability.

review.inputs: Account workspace registration, instance channel connection, app membership and reviewed message/artifact.
narrative: Slack publication is one-way in the documented preview. Registration authorizes the workspace; the instance connection selects a channel; channel membership permits delivery. Posting does not establish channel reading, command handling or thread interaction.

There is no per-message approval prompt, including interactive requests. Review the intended channel and content before invocation, then inspect actual delivery. Disconnecting the channel is not a mechanism for deleting previously posted messages.
configuration: Add the app to the channel; instance → Add connection → Slack; select integration and channel ID.
Use the reviewed destination and verify the resulting post.
lifecycle: Message may be sent without an approval prompt.
Future access changes; existing posts remain externally managed.
review.controls: Review audience before sending. The integration does not provide general edit/delete, channel administration or conversation reading.
review.observable_output: Actual channel post and recorded action/delivery result.
review.undocumented: Deduplicated retries, universal rollback and guaranteed post deletion are not provided by the documented interface.
test: Use a restricted test channel containing the installed app.
Verify destination and content without expecting a confirmation prompt.
Remove app membership for an authorized negative test and distinguish delivery failure from task failure.

claims.assertion: Connections are per-instance/channel and one-way; membership is required.
Posting does not prompt for approval even in interactive invocation.

entries.title: Built-in operational inquiry
entries.state: Request context and connected source evidence
entries.process: Use the built-in on-demand inquiry path to answer the operational question using available authorized evidence.
entries.verification: Inspect scope and reproduce a material observation from the same source query.
entries.on_failure: Name the missing source and qualify or withhold the answer; creating a custom agent does not by itself repair source access.

review.inputs: Explicit question, service/account scope, observation interval and connected evidence.
narrative: The built-in inquiry path answers an operational question without requiring a separately created custom agent. It still depends on the Agent Space sources and permissions. Use a custom definition for a recurring or specialized procedure; configure source access independently.
The response is scoped to evidence actually available to that request. Record the queried period and reproduce a material observation before treating a health summary as an operational fact.
configuration: Open Chat in the intended Agent Space and state service identifiers and UTC interval.
Check relevant source associations and permission scope.
lifecycle: Response or source gap is produced.
A new configuration path, not automatic conversion.
review.controls: A conversational request is not permission for a state-changing operation.
review.observable_output: Scoped answer and available supporting tool observations.
review.undocumented: The cited guide does not specify the query-selection algorithm. Inspect the sources and query parameters used by the execution.
test: Ask for one known staging service measurement in a complete interval.
Compare it with the monitoring source.
An unavailable metric must be listed as missing rather than inferred as healthy.

claims.section: Custom agents compared to built-in capabilities
claims.assertion: On-demand queries are a built-in path; custom agents are separately configured.

claims.section: Configuring MCP tools in an Agent Space
claims.assertion: Connected evidence remains subject to selected source tools.

entries.title: Finding-edit personalization
entries.trigger: Eligible edits from the most recent completed test when personalization was enabled at test start
entries.state: Retained finding preferences and original/latest finding attributes
entries.process: Apply eligible learned preferences to similar findings in subsequent penetration-test runs.
entries.verification: Inspect original/latest values and the Personalization changes explanation separately from vulnerability evidence.
entries.on_failure: Treat unobserved personalization as unverified; a severity change does not establish a repaired application.

review.inputs: Eligible operator edits in the most recent completed penetration-test run and Findings Personalization enabled when the test starts.
narrative: Findings Personalization learns eligible edits and applies preferences to similar findings on later runs. It is distinct from discovering vulnerabilities, retaining a login procedure and replaying a finding. Learned changes can alter finding attributes without proving that application behavior changed.

Inspect the Personalization changes explanation and original values before interpreting a severity change. For status, the documented learnable signal is marking a finding FALSE_POSITIVE; other status updates are not equivalent learning inputs.
configuration: Inspect Findings Personalization in the penetration-test configuration; documented default is enabled.
Must be enabled at test start for learning
Review edits in the most recent completed run.
Not arbitrary edits from all historical runs
Compare original/latest attributes and Personalization changes where shown.
lifecycle: Similar findings can receive personalized attributes.
Most recent edit replaces the earlier preference.
Raw agent-produced findings are shown; preferences remain retained.
review.controls: Personalized severity is not evidence of a repaired vulnerability. Disabling the feature is not deleting learned preferences.
review.observable_output: Original/latest attributes and a Personalization changes explanation on affected findings.
review.undocumented: Similarity thresholds, internal preference storage and a public preference CRUD resource are not established by the guide.
test: Use a controlled staging finding whose risk context can be changed without modifying the application.
Inspect whether a later similar finding exposes the personalization change.
Disable personalization; compare raw output without claiming that retained preferences were deleted.

claims.section: How personalization learns from your edits; Enable or disable Findings Personalization
claims.assertion: Learning uses eligible edits from the most recent completed run; false-positive status is special, and disabling preserves preferences.
